attempt1_at_100_in_flight.definition: pooled over attempt 1's three repeats: median server latency of 200s that arrived with 90..110 in flight on the engine, the arriving one included; references are the curve's and the maxseqs128 host's median latencies, linearly interpolated to 100 between measured levels

host_speed.calibrated_ratios_note: per calibrated validation repeat, in repeat order: the host's median server latency over the curve's at that concurrency
host_speed.curve_hosts_source: data/a2/service-sweep.jsonl (ok runs; the curve file names no host)
host_speed.engine_version_source: engine.vllm_version of every record in data/a2/service-sweep.jsonl and data/a2/exploratory/maxseqs*.jsonl; the validation records carry none

hosts_in_records.definition: distinct host ids across the curve's runs (service-sweep), the host re-measurement (exploratory) and every validation repeat, void ones included; measured_for_speed counts those with a closed-loop latency: the curve's host, the re-measured host and the calibrated attempt's host

host_speed.note: hosts are the RunPod worker ids the findings doc already names; host ids are published, probe worker ids are not

lb_502_first_attempt_s.source: the a2-driver-lb-retry header value '502:<seconds>' on rows of probes 3, 4, 5

load_balancer.lb_502_first_attempt_validation_s_why: the validation records keep only the indices of retried requests (lb_502_retried), not the retry header's value, so the first attempt's duration was not recorded for any validation repeat
load_balancer.per_worker_concurrency_note: server intervals reconstructed: each ends return_leg_s before the client saw the response and lasts the stamped server latency (autoscale.a2_evidence)

probe2_502_s.source: probe 2's rows with status 502 and no x-a2-worker header (probe 2 did not retry them); their client latency

1.status: stopped: RuntimeError: can't start new thread

load_balancer.probes_1_to_3_distinct_workers_note: x-a2-worker ids across the steps and summary of probes 1, 2 and 3, counted; the ids are not published

stall_share.definition: share_over_threshold: completed requests over threshold_s client-side; share_client_minus_server_over_threshold: client minus server latency over threshold_s (time outside the engine); share_of_over_threshold_with_server_over: of the requests over threshold_s client-side, those whose server latency is over server_backlog_s (time inside the engine)

void: 2 requests without a 200 (0 of them transport errors)

money.gpu_rate_caveat: RunPod's reported rate for that worker, not cross-checked against billing; artifact 4's recon (docs/recon-a4.md) implied $1.106/h for a flex serverless RTX 4090 worker, so the billed rate may differ; the spend record (docs/spend-a2.md) is the billing
money.list_over_reported_definition: the pricing page's serverless rate over the reported costPerHr; every dollar figure scales by it

load_balancer_cap.ratio_definition: scaler 128's delivered rate over scaler 4's, which is also scaler 4's cost per request over scaler 128's (same workers, same hourly rate)
load_balancer_cap.scaler_128_source: probe 3 (scaler value 128), delivered rate at the 300 req/s step
load_balancer_cap.scaler_4_source: probe 1 (scaler value 4), median of its steps' delivered rates; the 100 req/s step ended on client-side errors

signal_choice.label: UNVALIDATED: simulator failed validation twice; p99s differ by 82 ms
signal_choice.p99_spread_definition: highest minus lowest reached p99 over the three signals on this sweep

simulator.campaign_runs_definition: records in data/campaign.jsonl, every arm, before any exclusion

h1.definition: holds only if it holds on both step arms

h2.definition: holds only if it holds on both arms and both shapes

h2_censoring.cap_cost_definition: one initial replica for the window plus one more at every cooldown from the first evaluation (t = evaluate_every) up to max_replicas, none removed: until + sum over k = 0..max_replicas-2 of (until - evaluate_every - k * cooldown)
h2_censoring.reading: the curve's GPU utilisation is at least 1 at every measured level, above the highest utilisation scale-up threshold (0.95), so the utilisation controller scales up at every chance; every utilisation run's cost equals the cap cost

h2_noise._note: at-cap utilisation policies run the same fleet (every run at the cap cost) but differ in median p99 because autoscale.sweep._derive_seed seeds a trace by (seed, scale_up_at, scale_down_at, repetition), not by signal, so policies with different thresholds replay different traces
h2_noise.h2_margin_definition: utilisation's reached p99 minus the highest reached p99 of the other two signals, signed; H2 holds exactly when it exceeds tie_seconds
h2_noise.margin_vs_best_other_definition: utilisation's reached p99 minus the lowest reached p99 of the other two signals, signed

h2_sensitivity.definition: H2 with utilization_throughput (the 'sensitivity <sweep>' sources) in utilisation's place; queue depth and in-flight frontiers are the headline's, and the iso-cost budget is recomputed for the set
